findings.title: Runner._run_subprocess leaks 'running' row on shlex.split ValueError
findings.description: _run_subprocess at runner.py:554-568 calls `shlex.split(command)` inside a try block that only catches `FileNotFoundError`. A `ValueError` from unbalanced quotes / trailing backslash propagates out of _run_subprocess BEFORE the row-finalisation block at runner.py:589-590 executes, so the in-memory row stays in status='running' forever. The previous hunt fixed the equivalent FR-02 path (`_execute_command`) but missed this FR-08 path (Runner.submit → _run_with_limit → _execute_assigned → _run_subprocess).
findings.code_snippet:
try:
            arglist = shlex.split(command)
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                *arglist,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            )
        except FileNotFoundError:
            row["status"] = "failed"
            row["exit_code"] = 127
            ...
            return
findings.reasoning: runner.py:554: shlex.split raises ValueError on unbalanced quotes ('echo "unbalanced'). The except clause at runner.py:561 only catches FileNotFoundError. The ValueError propagates up through _execute_assigned and _run_with_limit, releasing the semaphore but never marking the row as failed. Confirmed via direct script: after `await runner.submit('echo "unbalanced')` + `await runner.drain()`, `runner.list_runs(task_id)` returns a row with status='running' indefinitely. The FR-02 _execute_command path (runner.py:240-249) was fixed in the previous hunt but the FR-08 _run_subprocess path (runner.py:554-568) has the same bug pattern and was not covered.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the FR-02 pattern: add `except ValueError:` block after `except FileNotFoundError:` that marks row status='failed', exit_code=-1, finished_at, duration_ms and returns early. Verified: ffec69d.
findings.verify_evidence: Direct repro: PYTHONPATH=src python -c '... await runner.submit(task_id, "echo \"unbalanced"); await runner.drain(); print(runner.list_runs(task_id))' returns [{'status': 'running', ...}]. After fix: [{'status': 'failed', 'exit_code': -1, 'finished_at': '<iso>', 'duration_ms': N}].

findings.title: T-01 tampering: SQL injection via string-concatenated SQL — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: SQL injection via string-concatenated SQL or unparameterised queries. owner_module = taskq_api.repository.session; boundary = TB-03.
findings.reasoning: Verified: session.py uses SQLAlchemy ORM/parameterised queries throughout. _build_engine (line 27-41) constructs an Engine via sqlalchemy.create_engine — the URL string flows into SQLAlchemy's parser (no string concatenation at the call site). transactional() (line 53-74) yields a Session for the repo helpers. task_repo (helpers at task_repo.py:24-53) calls store.insert/get/list_paginated/delete — all duck-typed through the in-memory store (test) or ORM (production). No string-concatenated SQL on any repo path. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: session.py:27-41 (_build_engine) and transactional (line 53-74) contain zero f-string SQL concatenation. repo helpers (task_repo.py:24-53) are duck-typed pass-throughs. search -rE 'execute\(f\"|execute\(\"%' in src/ returns no results.
findings.attack_vector: POST /v1/tasks with name/command containing SQL fragments (e.g. 'foo\'; DROP TABLE tasks; --') — the payload is validated by _no_injection regex (schemas.py:36-45) and stored as-is. The repository then issues parameterised SELECT/INSERT, so the SQL fragment never reaches the parser.
findings.attempted_exploit: Attacker submits name="x'; DROP TABLE tasks; --" via POST /v1/tasks. TaskCreate._command_safe rejects on '[;&|`$<>\\]\r' (semicolon blocked). Even if accepted, task_repo.insert calls store.insert(row) which uses parameterised SQL.

resolution.refute_evidence: N/A — threat mitigation verified. No code change required.

findings.title: T-02 spoofing: API key brute-force/replay against X-API-Key — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: API key brute-force / replay against the X-API-Key header. owner_module = taskq_api.service.auth; boundary = TB-01.
findings.reasoning: Verified: verify_key uses SHA-256 hash dict lookup. Brute-force against the hash space is infeasible (2^256 keys); the dict lookup is O(1) but the hash input space prevents enumeration. Replay protection relies on TLS at the transport layer (not enforced at the application layer — out of scope for SAD §6). Confirmed: T-02 mitigation effective.
findings.suggested_fix: N/A — mitigation in place (SHA-256 dict lookup).
findings.verify_evidence: auth.py:78 hash_key(presented_key.encode()).hexdigest() returns 64-char hex SHA-256. auth.py:79 find_by_hash(digest) → key_repo.lookup_by_hash → dict hit. Brute-force on hash: 2^256 input space, infeasible. Replay: TLS is the documented boundary (TB-01).
findings.attack_vector: Attacker iterates X-API-Key values to find a valid key. Attacker captures a request over plaintext HTTP and replays the header.
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: for k in <rainbow>; do curl -H "X-API-Key: $k" /v1/tasks; done — each request hits auth.py:78 hash_key then auth.py:79 find_by_hash (O(1) dict miss → 401). No rate limit on the 401 path, but enumeration is constrained by 2^256 input space. Replay requires TLS to be terminated.

findings.title: T-03 elevation_of_privilege: Subprocess command injection — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: Subprocess command injection via shell metacharacters. owner_module = taskq_api.service.runner; boundary = TB-04.
findings.code_snippet:
try:
    arglist = shlex.split(command)
    proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
        *arglist,
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    )
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-03 mitigation is three-layer: (1) TaskCreate._no_injection (schemas.py:36-45) rejects shell metachars [&|`$<>\\], $(), backticks; (2) shlex.split parses the command into argv tokens; (3) asyncio.create_subprocess_exec (NOT shell=True) uses execve so argv is passed verbatim to the kernel. Confirmed: shell metacharacters cannot escape the argv array. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: schemas.py:29-33 _INJECTION_PATTERNS rejects ';&|`$<>\\]\r' + '$\(' + '`'. runner.py:226 / 555 shlex.split + runner.py:227 / 556 create_subprocess_exec(*arglist) — exec form, no shell.
findings.attack_vector: POST /v1/tasks with command='echo hello; rm -rf /' — semicolon blocked by validator. Even if accepted, shlex.split would parse to ['echo', 'hello;', 'rm', '-rf', '/'] (literal tokens, not shell).
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: curl -d '{"name":"x","command":"echo hi; touch /tmp/pwned"}' — semicolon ';' is in [;&|`$<>\\]\r blocklist (schemas.py:29), rejected at 422 before reaching runner.

findings.title: T-04 denial_of_service: Rate-limit race allowing over-admission — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: Rate-limit race condition allowing over-admission. owner_module = taskq_api.repository.rate_repo; boundary = TB-02.
findings.code_snippet:
def try_consume(token: str, *, now: float, burst: int, per_sec: float) -> Tuple[bool, float]:
    _ensure_schema()
    with _get_engine().begin() as conn:
        row = conn.execute(text(_select_sql()), {"token": token}).first()
findings.reasoning: Verified: rate_repo.try_consume uses a single engine.begin() transaction (rate_repo.py:267) with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on Postgres/MySQL/MSSQL (rate_repo.py:63-66) and StaticPool+begin() on SQLite. test_fr05_parallel_double_burst_no_over_admission exercises 2*burst concurrent requests against the same token and asserts exactly `burst` admissions. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.suggested_fix: N/A — row-level lock + transactional update in place.
findings.verify_evidence: rate_repo.py:267 'with _get_engine().begin() as conn' opens a single transaction; rate_repo.py:64 _SELECT_FOR_UPDATE_SQL emits 'SELECT ... FOR UPDATE' for non-SQLite dialects; rate_repo.py:96-97 StaticPool serialises SQLite. test_fr05.py:337-386 passes (2*burst concurrent → exactly burst admitted).
findings.attack_vector: Attacker fires N>burst parallel requests from the same X-API-Key token. With naive read-then-write, two concurrent calls could both read tokens=burst, both write tokens=burst-1, leading to over-admission.
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: parallel -j $((burst*2)) curl -H 'X-API-Key: <token>' /v1/tasks — test_fr05_parallel_double_burst_no_over_admission verifies the row lock holds: exactly `burst` admit, the rest get 429.

findings.title: T-05 information_disclosure: 403 reveals resource existence — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: 403 response reveals whether a resource exists. owner_module = taskq_api.api.deps; boundary = TB-01.
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-05 mitigation is two-layer: (1) require_scope("admin") dep (deps.py:81-97) runs BEFORE the delete_task_endpoint handler (api/tasks.py:132-153), so the 403 is raised before the handler queries the DB; (2) errors.py:74 _INSTANCE_SCRUB_STATUSES = frozenset({403}) — _resolve_instance (errors.py:155-160) returns '' for 403 so the request URL path is scrubbed. The body detail is 'insufficient scope' (no resource id leak). mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: deps.py:58-60 raise problem(403, 'Forbidden', 'insufficient scope') — generic detail, no resource id. errors.py:155-160 _resolve_instance returns '' when status in _INSTANCE_SCRUB_STATUSES (frozenset({403})). The DELETE handler (api/tasks.py:132) never runs when 403 fires.
findings.attack_vector: Attacker probes DELETE /v1/tasks/{id} with a valid write key. If id exists, response would reveal 404 vs 403 (resource leak).
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: curl -X DELETE -H 'X-API-Key: <write-key>' /v1/tasks/<random-uuid> — require_scope('admin') raises 403 (no DB query) regardless of whether task_id exists.

findings.title: T-06 information_disclosure: Error body leaks stack trace / SQL / path — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: Error body leaks stack trace, SQL, or file path. owner_module = taskq_api.errors; boundary = TB-05.
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-06 mitigation is enforced in errors.py:281-282 (generic 500 fallback returns 'internal server error' — NOT exc text) and errors.py:268-280 (StarletteHTTPException path uses exc.status_code + canonical _STATUS_ENVELOPES detail, not raw text). test_fr10_forced_500_detail_leaks_no_internals asserts no internals leak. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: errors.py:281-282 'return 500, "Internal Server Error", "internal server error", {}' — generic message, no exc propagation. errors.py:268-269 RequestValidationError → 'request validation failed'. test_fr10.py:fr10_forced_500_detail_leaks_no_internals passes.
findings.attack_vector: Attacker triggers an unhandled exception (e.g. malformed request that bypasses validators), hoping the body leaks the original exception text (traceback, SQL, file paths).
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: curl -X POST /v1/foobar -d 'invalid json' — Starlette raises RequestValidationError → mapped to 422 + 'request validation failed' (no traceback). If an unhandled Exception fires, errors.py:281-282 returns 'internal server error'.

findings.title: T-07 information_disclosure: Plaintext API key / DB password leaks into logs — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: Plaintext API key or DB password leaks into logs / metrics. owner_module = taskq_api.errors; boundary = TB-03.
findings.code_snippet:
def _emit_log_line(*, status: int, correlation_id: str, instance: str, title: str) -> None:
    level = logging.WARNING if status >= 500 else logging.INFO
    _log.log(level, "request_outcome status=%d correlation_id=%s instance=%s title=%s",
             status, correlation_id, instance, title)
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-07 mitigation is enforced by (1) hash_key (auth.py:40-45) — plaintext is hashed on entry, never logged; (2) errors._emit_log_line (errors.py:182-204) emits only status, correlation_id, instance, title — no API key, no SQL, no DB password; (3) _log = logging.getLogger('taskq_api') is a fixed-name logger (no PII). mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: errors.py:182-204 _emit_log_line logs only status + correlation_id + instance + title. auth.py:40-45 hash_key never logs plaintext. Grep -rn 'log.*X-API-Key\|log.*api_key\|log.*DB_PASS' in src/ returns 0 matches.
findings.attack_vector: Attacker triggers verbose logging (e.g. by injecting a 500), hoping the structured log line includes X-API-Key or DB connection string.
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: trigger 500 via malformed request → inspect stderr/log capture → confirm log line contains only status/correlation_id/instance/title (no secret).

findings.title: T-08 denial_of_service: Child subprocess becomes orphan on timeout — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: Child subprocess becomes orphan on timeout. owner_module = taskq_api.service.runner; boundary = TB-04.
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-08 mitigation — _terminate (runner.py:196-213) does kill+wait; on TimeoutError (runner.py:269 / runner.py:581) the runner calls _terminate to reap the subprocess before returning. kill sends SIGKILL (uncatchable); wait() blocks until kernel reaps. NP-15 invariant pinned by tests. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: runner.py:269 / runner.py:581 'except asyncio.TimeoutError: await _terminate(proc)' — kill+wait on every timeout. runner.py:206-213 _terminate: proc.kill() (SIGKILL) + await proc.wait() (reap).
findings.attack_vector: Attacker submits a long-running command ('sleep infinity') that exceeds task_timeout, hoping the subprocess becomes a zombie after the HTTP response is finalised.
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: curl POST /v1/tasks/{id}/run with task_timeout=1 — runner.py:259-261 asyncio.wait_for fires TimeoutError, runner.py:270 _terminate kill+wait reaps the child before returning.

findings.title: T-09 denial_of_service: asyncio.CancelledError swallowed on shutdown — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: asyncio.CancelledError swallowed on shutdown causes graceful drain to hang. owner_module = taskq_api.service.runner; boundary = TB-02.
findings.code_snippet:
async def _run_body(self, body: Any) -> Any:
    return await body()

async def _run_with_limit(self, task_id, run_id, command, timeout):
    await self._semaphore.acquire()
    try:
        ...
        await self._execute_assigned(...)
    finally:
        self._semaphore.release()
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-09 mitigation — _run_body (runner.py:473-483) has NO try/except around body(); _run_with_limit only has try/finally for semaphore release (no except clause); _execute_assigned only has try/finally for _in_flight decrement. asyncio.CancelledError inherits from BaseException (Python 3.8+) and slips past `except Exception` if any were present — but no `except Exception` exists on these paths, so CancelledError propagates cleanly. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: runner.py:483 'return await body()' — no try/except. runner.py:503-511 await + try/finally (no except). runner.py:533-536 try/finally (no except). test_fr10_shutdown_drain_cancels_over_budget_tasks verifies cancellation propagates and marks rows interrupted.
findings.attack_vector: Attacker / operator initiates FastAPI shutdown while tasks are running, hoping CancelledError is swallowed by a defensive try/except, causing shutdown_drain to hang.
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: shutdown sequence → shutdown_drain awaits _tasks via asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True) → cancelled tasks raise CancelledError → bubbles up to FastAPI lifespan shutdown → process exits cleanly within drain budget.

findings.title: T-10 repudiation: Client actions not correlated across logs and responses — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: Client actions cannot be correlated across logs and responses. owner_module = taskq_api.errors; boundary = TB-01.
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-10 mitigation — _generate_correlation_id (errors.py:121-143) re-uses inbound X-Correlation-Id header (echoing client-provided trace id) or mints UUID4; the same correlation_id is set on (1) the response body field, (2) the X-Correlation-Id response header (errors.py:233), (3) the structured log line (errors.py:198-204). Client traces and server logs share one join key. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.verify_evidence: errors.py:143 UUID4 fallback. errors.py:233 X-Correlation-Id header mirrors body. errors.py:198-204 _emit_log_line logs the same correlation_id. test_fr10_correlation_id_header_matches_body + test_fr10_correlation_id_appears_in_server_log pass.
findings.attack_vector: Operator wants to correlate a client-reported failed request with the server-side log line; without a join key the trace is unsearchable.
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: curl -H 'X-Correlation-Id: trace-123' POST /v1/tasks → response body['correlation_id'] == 'trace-123' AND X-Correlation-Id header == 'trace-123' AND log line contains 'correlation_id=trace-123'.

findings.title: T-11 tampering: v3 migration data loss on downgrade path — mitigation verified
findings.description: STRIDE-lite threat from SAD §6: v3 migration data loss on downgrade path. owner_module = migrations.versions.v3_split_results; boundary = TB-03.
findings.reasoning: Verified: T-11 mitigation — upgrade() creates task_results, back-fills from tasks.result_json (the source column is NEVER dropped), downgrade() drops task_results only (tasks.result_json retains the payload). The pre-existing v3_split_results#1 finding (low, open in the previous report) documents that a backfill IntegrityError on duplicate tasks.id is now handled: op.drop_table('task_results') on line 88 unwinds the CREATE before re-raising, so the migration is all-or-nothing. mitigation_effective=true.
findings.suggested_fix: N/A — mitigation in place (downgrade does not touch tasks.result_json).
findings.verify_evidence: v3_split_results.py:72-94 upgrade: create_table + backfill + try/except rollback. v3_split_results.py:97-107 downgrade: drop_table('task_results') — tasks.result_json column untouched. test_fr07_v3_downgrade_preserves_result_json + test_fr07_v3_backfill_rollback_on_integrity_error cover both directions.
findings.attack_vector: Operator runs `alembic downgrade -1` to roll back v3, hoping the data move destroys tasks.result_json.
findings.attempted_exploit: Bash: alembic downgrade -1 → downgrade() drops task_results; tasks.result_json column was never modified by upgrade(), so the payload is intact. Upgrade again restores task_results with the same rows.

findings.title: Backfill can leave migration in partial state on IntegrityError (carry-over from previous hunt)
findings.description: v3_split_results.py:84-94 — if the backfill INSERT into task_results fails (e.g. duplicate task_id from data corruption), the try/except block drops task_results before re-raising. The drop ensures the upgrade is all-or-nothing on a transactional DDL backend. On a non-transactional backend (e.g. older MySQL), the CREATE TABLE may persist while the data move is rolled back — leaving the schema in a half-applied state.
findings.reasoning: v3_split_results.py:84-94 — backfill IntegrityError → drop_table('task_results') → raise. The drop ensures transactional backends (Postgres, SQLite) leave no trace. For non-transactional DDL (older MySQL with autocommit DDL) the CREATE TABLE survives the rollback, leaving the schema half-applied. Low severity because production uses a transactional DDL backend.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: add ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING to the INSERT (defense in depth). Not blocking Gate 3.
findings.verify_evidence: v3_split_results.py:88 op.drop_table is the rollback hook. The scenario requires non-transactional DDL — out of scope for the current production backend.

resolution.refute_evidence: N/A — carried over from previous hunt as low. Defense-in-depth only; not blocking.
